item.title: [junegunn/fzf] 0.75.0
item.description:
junegunn/fzf | 84055 stars| 4118 forks.

| Makefile | Go | Ruby | Shell | Dockerfile | PowerShell | Assembly | Nushell | Vim Script |

:cherry_blossom: A command-line fuzzy finder
  • Added {change,transform,bg-transform}-info-command actions (#4951) (@casperdcl) 
    seq 100 | fzf --info-command 'echo "mode: A | $FZF_INFO"' \
              --bind 'ctrl-a:change-info-command:echo "mode: A | $FZF_INFO"' \
              --bind 'ctrl-b:change-info-command:echo "mode: B | $FZF_INFO"'
  • transform-nth and transform-with-nth (and their bg- variants) no longer split the output at |
    • Only change-nth and change-with-nth rotate through |-separated values
    • Fixed the bound command being replaced with the output. e.g. With transform-nth(echo '1|2'), the next key press ran 2|1 as a shell command.
    • A --with-nth template in the output can now contain |. e.g. {2}|{1} was cut to {2}.
  • change-nth and transform-nth now handle empty and invalid values the same way as change-with-nth and transform-with-nth
    • An empty value restores the default --nth. Previously, change-nth() and an empty transform-nth output searched all fields. Use change-nth(..) for that.
    • A non-empty invalid value is ignored. Previously, it restored the default --nth.
  • change-nth and change-with-nth now apply the value after the current one in the |-separated list
    • A value equal to the current one is skipped, e.g. the first value when it is the initial --nth
    • Invalid values in the list are skipped
    • The rotation follows the current value even when another binding changed it, or when the action is printed by transform (unless the list contains the same value more than once)
    • You can list the values in their natural order, starting with the initial one 
      # Previously, you would have to write:
ls -al | fzf --with-nth .. --bind 'space:change-with-nth:1|2|..'

# Now you can write:
ls -al | fzf --with-nth .. --bind 'space:change-with-nth:..|1|2'
  • Fixed --no-sort being ignored in filter mode with --sync, --tac, or --bench (#4940) (@NavpreetSSidhu)
  • Fixed --walker=follow skipping a symlink in one --walker-root when its target is an ancestor of another root (#4944) (@mabunemeh)
  • Fixed data races in the preview and the search result cache (#4947)
  • Fixed O(n^2) action parsing in --listen. A single ~1 MB request could block the server for ~30 s (@zachariah-mithani, AploSec)
  • Windows

item.title: [meta/flow] v0.339.0
item.description:
meta/flow | 22310 stars| 1890 forks.

| Shell | JavaScript | Makefile | Ruby | CSS | Vim Snippet | TypeScript | Rust | RenderScript | MDX |

Adds static typing to JavaScript to improve developer productivity and code quality.

Breaking Changes:

  • Rename typeParameters to typeArguments on ESTree GenericTypeAnnotation, InterfaceExtends, and ClassImplements, including WASM flow-parser output. Declaration parameters and Babel output retain their existing names.
  • PropertyDescriptor and Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor are no longer generic. Remove type arguments from PropertyDescriptor<T> annotations and Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor<T>(...) calls.

Likely to cause new Flow errors:

  • Hook calls in classes now use react-rule-hook-class, and calls in deeper nested anonymous callbacks inside components or hooks use react-rule-hook-conditional, instead of react-rule-hook. Update suppressions to the new codes. Hook calls directly in class property initializers are also rejected when the enclosing function would otherwise permit them.
  • Assignments and throws in function or component parameter defaults and destructuring defaults are now treated as conditional, because a default only runs when the value it replaces is undefined.
  • Property increments and decrements (o.x++, o.x--, ++o.x, and --o.x) now invalidate narrowings of the property through aliases, as assignments already do.
  • Reads in an assertion call's condition now use the types at the point where they run, rather than types after the call and its later arguments. This removes false errors and reports reads before a later argument assigns a variable.
  • break, continue, return, and throw paths through finally are no longer dropped. Flow now reports variables left unassigned and narrowings that do not hold on these paths.
  • Optional class fields (x?: T, with experimental.tslib_syntax) now have type T | void. Reads may return undefined, and assigning undefined is allowed.
  • Type parameters explicitly declared in out in TypeScript files are now invariant rather than covariant.
  • Functions named use* declared in TypeScript files are now treated as hooks. This fixes calls from Flow hook syntax, but calls outside a component or hook can now report Rules of Hooks errors.
  • parseInt, parseFloat, and eval now require a string; isNaN and isFinite require a number; and builtin Error constructors require a string message, matching TypeScript.
  • Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor, Object.defineProperty, Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty, and Object.prototype.propertyIsEnumerable now require PropertyKey (string | number | symbol) keys. PropertyDescriptorMap is also keyed by PropertyKey.
  • DataView.byteLength and byteOffset, numeric typed array byteLength, byteOffset, and length, and RegExp.source, global, ignoreCase, and multiline are now read-only. RegExp.prototype.compile now requires a pattern.
  • Array.prototype.splice uses separate removal and insertion overloads, so inserting items requires a deleteCount.
  • Array and ReadonlyArray reduce and reduceRight now have an overload whose initial value and accumulator use the element type. Calls intending a different accumulator type may need an explicit type argument, e.g. reduce<number>(...).
  • Promise.prototype.then and catch now use TypeScript-style signatures. then has separate fulfillment and rejection type parameters; calls whose inferred result is unsuitable may need explicit type arguments.
  • RegExpMatchArray.index and input are now optional, and its first element is declared as 0: string. Check optional fields on match results, and use RegExpExecArray for exec and matchAll results.
  • Error.stack is now optional, matching TypeScript.
  • Numeric typed array subarray methods, including Uint8Array.prototype.subarray, return their corresponding typed array rather than this. Subclasses that return their own type should declare their own override.

New Features:

  • Format code with Prettier in the Try Flow playground, and copy JSON from its AST view.
  • Object type spreads allow optional properties after an object with an indexer. Value spreads retain their existing checks.
  • Add translateFlowTypeToTSType to flow-api-translator for type-node translation.
  • Functions with any return type are accepted where a TypeScript-declared function type returning void is expected, matching TypeScript. Flow-declared function types retain their existing return checks.

Notable bug fixes:

  • Fixed Windows commands such as flow check hanging when their output is piped or captured, even after the command exits (#9519).
  • Preserve imported TypeScript template literal types without requiring experimental.tslib_syntax.
  • Type guards refine distinct bigint literal types to empty, as they already do for string, number, and boolean literals.
  • Fixed an internal error when a function parameter default always throws; the function is now typed and checked.
  • JavaScript objects with extra properties can be checked against TypeScript object types whose index signature applies to only some keys, and against interfaces extending an object type with an index signature.
  • Accept literal initializers such as declare const x = -1.
  • Improve implicit instantiation through conditional types without infer, conditional types nested inside distributive conditional types, and type applications that expand to types mentioning the inferred parameters.
  • Fixed a crash when a mapped type's key has the same name as a type parameter spread in the mapped object type.
  • Imports such as .//foo and ..//foo resolve like ./foo and ../foo.
  • Prevent stack overflows and spurious internal errors when checking recursive tuple spreads in generic type arguments.
  • JavaScript subclasses can override static methods of TypeScript classes with narrower parameters, as on the instance side.
  • Fixed a crash on a match in unreachable code.
  • Fixed a crash when a namespace merged with a class or function redeclares one of its members.
  • Fixed crashes when a recheck is canceled while checking a component declaration, or when cancellation or a timeout interrupts a type cast from an annotated source.
  • Fixed a crash on a method with a this parameter in a class expression or a class declared in a callback.
  • Fixed a crash when a file imports a name that it also declares as a function, component, or hook.
  • Fixed crashes when a library definition stops parsing while the server is running, or contains an ignored statement that reads a name, such as f();.
  • TypeScript enum checking no longer requires enums=true.
  • Fixed a crash ("Non speculating: LimitExceeded") when destructuring a value whose type lookup exceeds the recursion limit.
  • A type parameter whose bound mentions another type parameter no longer leaks unresolved into the other parameter's solution.
  • A field named constructor, including TypeScript's ['constructor'] fields, now types x.constructor without shadowing the constructor used by new and super().
  • Named imports work from CommonJS modules whose module.exports has multiple call signatures or is an overloaded function merged with a namespace.
  • Mapped types with template literal keys now produce individual properties when their placeholders resolve to string literals, instead of retaining a template literal indexer. Generic placeholders and unsupported intersection or recursive-alias cases retain their existing behavior.
  • flow-upgrade transformations preserve type arguments with both legacy and current parser AST fields.

Misc:

  • Implements errors print the implemented interface's type and type arguments instead of generic descriptions such as "exports".
  • Try Flow disables Clear and Copy code when the editor is empty, keeps the Format button stable as saved-state controls change, and places the AST format selector after its hide options.
  • Tooling documentation recommends flow-parser and Prettier's built-in Flow parser without an external parser plugin.

Parser:

  • Program source locations and ranges span the entire input, including whitespace and comments.
  • flow-parser preserves optionality on constructor parameter properties.
  • Correct flow-estree types for unannotated object type properties, readonly type operators, combined in out variance, optional Program.tokens, sparse-array elements, and JSX namespaced attributes. Sparse-array parent repair and traversal preserve holes.
  • Omit absent typeof type arguments from ESTree output, including WASM-decoded nodes and detached builders.
  • Default interface exports have the correct type-only export kind and AST typings. Type stripping removes the complete export wrapper rather than leaving a dangling export default.
  • flow-parser type stripping preserves function parameter defaults and side-effect imports.
  • flow-transform preserves leading #! lines.
  • flow-eslint scope analysis handles TypeScript parameter properties, class member decorators, and declare global.
  • Type translation preserves readonly array and tuple operands, inline interface bodies, and qualified interface bases.
  • Type translation tracks required React imports for JSX-qualified types.
  • Strict TypeScript translation rejects unsupported generic indexer keys instead of silently losing qualification or type arguments. Recovering string-API behavior is unchanged.

IDE:

  • Hover on calls to polymorphic functions, including functions bound by const, properties, or parameters, and on construction of polymorphic classes shows the instantiated type arguments.
  • Multiline unions and intersections in hover types are indented under their annotation, one member per line.
  • Hover, dump-types, and error messages print any without its kind, e.g. any instead of any (explicit).

Library Definitions:

  • encodeURIComponent also accepts numbers and booleans.
  • Symbol.prototype.valueOf returns symbol instead of ?symbol.
  • arguments.callee and Function.prototype.caller are typed as Function, and function prototype properties are typed as any.
  • TemplateStringsArray is an interface extending ReadonlyArray<string>.
  • Add ImportCallOptions, ImportAssertions, and ImportAttributes interfaces.
  • Date.prototype.toString declares a Date receiver rather than inheriting an Object receiver.
  • Locale-sensitive methods of String, Number, and Date use overloads and Intl option types.
  • Calling EvalError, RangeError, ReferenceError, SyntaxError, TypeError, or URIError returns its own type rather than Error.
  • JSON.parse reviver and JSON.stringify replacer callbacks accept any this and receive a string key.
  • JSON.stringify returns string; its replacer is a function or a read-only array of strings and numbers.
  • Declare legacy RegExp statics such as RegExp.$1 and RegExp.lastMatch.
  • ArrayBuffer.isView is a type guard that refines its argument to ArrayBufferView.
  • ArrayBufferView is a structural interface rather than a union of typed arrays and DataView. Libraries can extend ArrayBufferTypes to add buffer types to ArrayBufferLike.
  • Add PromiseConstructorLike and ConcatArray.
  • Add the ThisType<T> marker interface. Flow does not give it TypeScript's contextual this behavior.
  • Numeric typed array callbacks accept thisArg?: any, and their static from methods accept mapping functions from any element type.
  • Libraries can redeclare ReactDOM$UserVisibleString to change the type accepted by user-visible React DOM string attributes such as aria-label, title, alt, and placeholder.
  • Boolean() accepts no argument.
  • Object.defineProperty and Object.defineProperties return their first argument's type.
  • Object.getPrototypeOf, Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor, Object.getOwnPropertyNames, Object.getOwnPropertySymbols, Object.isSealed, Object.isFrozen, and Object.isExtensible accept any argument.
  • Object.prototype.valueOf returns Object instead of unknown.
  • String.prototype.matchAll yields RegExpExecArray for string patterns as well as regular expressions.

item.title: [rendro/vintageJS] v2.5.0
item.description:
rendro/vintageJS | 844 stars| 111 forks.

| TypeScript |

Add a retro/vintage effect to images using the HTML5 canvas element

Film grain and light leaks

Two new effects, both optional and backwards compatible.

vintagejs(photo, {
  grain: 0.35,                                  // 0–1
  lightLeak: { intensity: 0.5, edge: 'left' },  // edge: left | right | top | bottom
});
  • grain: film grain that shows most in the midtones. It scales with the image size, so a small preview and the full-size photo look the same, and it is identical on every run (no flicker between renders).
  • lightLeak: a warm glow bleeding in from one edge, like light getting into an old camera. Optional color (default warm orange).
  • New exported types: TLightLeak, TLightLeakEdge, TRGBColor.
  • Tests now render real pixels in Node via @napi-rs/canvas.

item.title: [wekan/wekan] v13.00
item.description:
wekan/wekan | 21159 stars| 3004 forks.

| HTML | JavaScript | Cap'n Proto | Shell | Dockerfile | Batchfile | Python | Pug | CSS | C |

FLOSS kanban, built with Meteor. Official Public Support at GitHub issues only. Official Private Pre-Paid Support at https://wekan.fi/commercial-support/ only. Translation PRs to imports/i18n/data/en.i18n.json, other translations at https://app.transifex.com/wekan/wekan . No telemetry.

In short

CreateBleed is fixed: "Only admins can create boards" now
holds on every path that creates a board - the browser console, the REST API,
imports, copies, clones and cards - not only on the Add Board form. The REST
API documentation spells the name WeKan, so the API pages published on
wekan.fi pass its brand-spelling check again.

Security

Only admins create boards on every path, not only through Add Board. Thanks to tsurutanmen and xet7.

CreateBleed,
GHSA-qcfm-2g4w-wqcc.
Admin Panel / Settings / Visibility / "Only admins can create boards"
(#4475) was checked only inside
createBoardWithInitialSwimlanes, the Add Board form. A user who is not an
admin still created working boards with a console Boards.insert - the
board collection's allow rule approves any signed-in user - with
POST /api/boards and with both board import routes, as reported, and also
with importBoard, cloneBoard, copyBoard, POST /api/boards/:boardId/copy
and createBoardFromCard. The boards belonged to their creator; no other
user's data was read or changed.

One decision (models/lib/boardCreationPolicy.js) and one guard
(server/lib/boardCreationGuard.js) are now asked by every one of those paths
before they write, and by a new Boards.deny insert rule. A board template
stays every member's own, and boards WeKan makes by itself - a user's
Templates board, a board's subtasks board - are not user creations. A refused
REST call answers 403. A refusal is recorded in Admin Panel / Problems as
CreateBleed (authz.board-creation, low, CWE-863, never disables the
account), and Duplicate and "Create board from card" are hidden like Add
Board, so only a client bypassing the interface reaches it.
tests/createBleed.test.cjs drives the decision, the guard and the real deny
rule against the reporter's console insert, and fails if any path that creates
a board for a user does not ask the guard, or if anything else reads the
setting; tests/playwright/specs/createbleed-board-creation-admin-only.e2e.js
replays the report against a running server.

Thanks to above GitHub users for their contributions.

More details at ChangeLog

item.title: [Automattic/harper] v3.1.0
item.description:
Automattic/harper | 17461 stars| 803 forks.

| Rust | JavaScript | CSS | HTML | Svelte | TypeScript | Dockerfile | C++ | Lua | Ruby |

Offline, privacy-first grammar checker. Fast, open-source, Rust-powered

What's Changed

Howdy! Today, I'm starting a new tradition for Harper. Instead of the bland, colorless release notes you've been receiving for past releases, you'll now be getting these new, awesome release notes I type up myself.

The hope is that by writing these notes directly, in addition to the updates on my blog, I can get closer to you guys, the people using Harper. I'll share some of the things on my mind, the places Harper is going, and the wonderful work Harper's community has gotten done since the last release.

We have a ton of updates and bug fixes coming in this release. I'll cover some of my favorite changes, but I won't be able to cover everything. You can find a list of ALL the changes in the PR notes at the end.

First off, we've simplified some parts of Harper's UI. In the desktop app, instead of seeing a green or red bar to signify if Harper is activated, you should see a dot below the Harper logo in the menu if the service is running. If the service is not running, there's no dot. Simple enough. You'll also observe that the menu bar should look much nicer in both light and dark modes. In the Chrome Extension, we've reverted some of the changes from v3.0.0 that made the popup menu (what you get when you click on the Harper logo) more "exciting". They were distracting and a little confusing, so we banished them.

Secondly, I've done a ton of work fixing bugs in our support for Google Docs. You should now see correct behavior when Harper checks sentences that span multiple pages and tables should now play more nicely with suggestions. Plus, thanks to @mvanhorn, we have some improved support for editors like WordPress' Gutenberg.

In the desktop app, we're pushing out some similar improvements. We got some reports that Harper didn't play well with setups with multiple monitors. It should be much cleaner now.

We also got some feedback that the Desktop app was a little confusing. We heard similar feedback a while ago about the Chrome Extension, which we addressed with a tip system. We set a similar "tip" system up for the Desktop app. We shall see if it help make things a little less confusing. From now on, you'll occasionally see tips appear when you review a highlighted problem in your text.

The most important changes, as always, were in our core grammar engine. We've added a ton of new rules and fixed a number of broken ones. Thanks to everyone who opened PRs in that vein, especially @hippietrail who's been reviewing them so prodigiously.

I'll talk to you again in the next release! Thanks for using Harper. Have a great weekend.

Best, Elijah Potter (@elijah-potter)

item.title: [emscripten-core/emscripten] 7.0.0
item.description:
emscripten-core/emscripten | 27759 stars| 3592 forks.

| CMake | Python | Shell | Makefile | HTML | JavaScript | C | C++ | Assembly | Batchfile |

Emscripten: An LLVM-to-WebAssembly Compiler

What's Changed

  • Remove support for the EMCC_ONLY_FORCED_STDLIBS environment variable, which
    was deprecated in 2.0.14 (#13448). Use -nostdlib instead to avoid linking
    standard libraries. (#28151)
  • libclang_rt.builtins and libclang_rt.profile are now linked directly into
    all side modules, matching upstream clang behaviour. This means they are
    no longer exported from the main module, reducing MAIN_MODULE=1 code size.
    A new system library, libemcc, now exists for the emscripten-specific code
    that was previously included in libclang_rt.builtins but requires a single
    program-wide definition. If you build with -nostdlib, and explictly list
    system libraries you would now need to include -lemcc. (#28142)
  • Split libclang_rt.profile out of libclang_rt.builtins so that it is only
    linked when profiling or coverage flags (such as -fprofile-instr-generate or
    --coverage) are enabled, avoiding unwanted default.profraw output at exit
    in MAIN_MODULE=1 builds. (#28123)
  • Pipes now have a 64 KiB capacity: non-blocking writes to a full pipe fail
    with EAGAIN. For now, blocking writes remain unbounded. (#27831)
  • When compiling and linking in a single command, auxiliary compiler output
    files (such as .dwo files from -gsplit-dwarf or .json files from
    -ftime-trace) are now named <output>-<input>.<ext>, matching the behavior
    of clang. Previously, .dwo files were named <input>.dwo and other
    auxiliary files were written to the temporary directory. (#28045)
  • libcxx, libcxxabi, libunwind and compiler-rt were updated to LLVM 23.1.3.
    Note that libc++ 23 removes many transitive header includes by default, which
    may cause build errors in code that relies on them. As a temporary workaround,
    you can define -D_LIBCPP_KEEP_TRANSITIVE_INCLUDES_LLVM23 until missing
    #include directives are added. See the libc++ 23 release notes for details:
    https://libcxx.llvm.org/ReleaseNotes/23.html#potentially-breaking-changes
    (#28011, #28014, #28108, #28149)
  • The WasmFS OPFS backend now uses readwrite-unsafe access handles in
    pthreads builds, so unlink and rename fail with EIO on files open
    read-only. (#27937)
  • mimalloc was updated to 3.6.1. (#28026, #28068, #28121)
  • Restored --whole-archive behaviour when linking with -sSIDE_MODULE=1
    (fixing a regression from 6.0.0 where static archives were no longer included
    in full), while keeping native archive behaviour for -shared. (#28055)
  • JavaScript library dependencies on other JavaScript library symbols are now
    detected automatically by the compiler, so __deps is no longer required for
    direct JS-to-JS references (__deps is still supported for dependencies on
    compiled C/C++ symbols or indirect dependencies). (#27995)
  • The default minimum browser versions targeted by Emscripten were increased:
    • MIN_CHROME_VERSION: 85 (Aug 2020) -> 93 (Aug 2021)
    • MIN_FIREFOX_VERSION: 79 (Jul 2020) -> 92 (Sep 2021)
    • MIN_SAFARI_VERSION: 15.0 (Sep 2021) -> 15.4 (Mar 2022)
      (#28141)

Contributors

Thanks to the following contributors: @sbc100 (70) @aheejin (7) @kleisauke (7) @clementperon (4) @guybedford (4) @dschuff (2) @JulesPatmanidis (2) @rustyconover (2) @tlively (2) @ypujante (2) @arsnyder16 (1) @basvandijk (1) @brendandahl (1) @dimokol (1) @Grantim (1) @hoodmane (1) @JesusFileto (1) @kripken (1) @lyrixx (1) @piandtheradians-glitch (1) @Project516 (1) @RagedPanda (1) @stephenduong1004 (1) @subhaushsingh (1) @Thanatos9404 (1) @trackoor (1)

item.title: [awslabs/aws-sdk-rust] November 6th, 2026
item.description:
awslabs/aws-sdk-rust | 3353 stars| 294 forks.

| Rust | JavaScript | TypeScript | Shell | Python |

AWS SDK for the Rust Programming Language

Service Features:

  • aws-sdk-athena (1.128.0): Added support for Athena System Tables which writes Athena usage data to AWS S3 managed tables in Apache Iceberg format. Adds CreateSystemTableConfiguration, UpdateSystemTableConfiguration, DeleteSystemTableConfiguration, GetSystemTableConfiguration, and ListSystemTableStatuses.
  • aws-sdk-autoscaling (1.141.0): Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling now lets you exclude managed resources from describe API responses using the new optional IncludeManagedResources parameter. Set this parameter to false to exclude managed resources from the response. By default, managed resources are included.
  • aws-sdk-bedrockagent (1.157.0): Add support for configuring searchability for metadata fields via UpdateKnowledgeBase request for Managed Knowledge Base. Once a field is marked as searchable it can be queried via query text and is factored into Managed Knowledge Base's ranking algorithm.
  • aws-sdk-connect (1.222.0): Rules in Amazon Connect now support ending email contacts associated to a case based on case events.
  • aws-sdk-connectcases (1.135.0): Amazon Connect Cases adds two Bulk Case Actions operations. BatchCreateRelatedItem adds a Comment-type related item to up to 100 cases per request, BatchUpdateCase updates fields (title, status, customer ID, custom) on up to 100 cases. Same domain, per-case success and failure results returned.
  • aws-sdk-datazone (1.168.0): Adds support for updating OAuth 2.0 connection settings with UpdateConnection.
  • aws-sdk-eksauth (1.118.0): Added workloadIdentityProviderArn to the AssumeRoleForPodIdentity API response.
  • aws-sdk-glue (1.184.0): Adds support for user-defined functions governed by AWS Lake Formation.
  • aws-sdk-lightsail (1.136.0): Marking fields as sensitive in GetInstanceAccessDetails, CreateKeyPair, DownloadDefaultKeyPair, CreateBucketAccessKey, CreateContainerServiceRegistryLogin, and GetRelationalDatabase responses.
  • aws-sdk-mediaconvert (1.154.0): Smart subtitling uses AWS Elemental Inference to generate captions from your content's audio, in embedded, burn-in, DVB-Sub, IMSC, SMI, SRT, teletext, TTML, or WebVTT outputs. Also fixes HEVC passthrough writing an incomplete codecs string to DASH and HLS manifests.
  • aws-sdk-ram (1.122.0): Adds support for using managed permission template parameters, discovering shared customer-managed permissions, and managing customer-managed permission deprecation.
  • aws-sdk-ssm (1.134.0): AWS Systems Manager now provides two new APIs - RegisterDefaultHostManagementConfiguration and DeregisterDefaultHostManagementConfiguration - along with a new DefaultHostManagementConfiguration CloudFormation resource type.

item.title: [apache/airflow] Apache Airflow 3.4.0
item.description:
apache/airflow | 47412 stars| 18322 forks.

| Python | JavaScript | CSS | HTML | Shell | Mako | Jupyter Notebook | Dockerfile | HCL | TypeScript |

Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

📦 PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/apache-airflow/3.4.0/
📚 Docs: https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/3.4.0/
🛠 Release Notes: https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/3.4.0/release_notes.html
🐳 Docker Image: "docker pull apache/airflow:3.4.0"
🚏 Constraints: https://github.com/apache/airflow/tree/constraints-3.4.0

Significant Changes

Task Loops (#73005, #74222, #74275, #74345)

Airflow 3.4.0 introduces Task Loops (AIP-111): a decorated task group can be repeated a number of
times decided at runtime using .loop(). A conditional loop works like a do ... while loop -
the body runs at least once and an until condition decides when to stop, bounded by
max_iterations. Each iteration can use the previous iteration's result and iterations run one
after another (tasks within an iteration can still run in parallel). Retried attempts are kept
under a per-attempt UUID so each iteration's data is preserved and can be cleared selectively.

For detailed usage instructions, see :doc:/authoring-and-scheduling/loops.

.. note::
Downgrading to any version earlier than 3.4.0 can be slow, depending on the number of
XCom rows that have been written after upgrading. Upgrading was tested on a
300m row XCom table, so please don't worry about upgrade time (we made sure
that the XCom data didn't get touched or read during migration to keep it
fast).

This is because this release contains a migration that starts storing new XCom
rows in an xcom_v2 table, and in order to downgrade we have to move those over
to the old table, and there is no way of doing this without copying the
written xcom values.

The downgrade refuses to continue when it finds data it cannot map back
safely. Each migration commits separately, so the later 3.4.0 migrations
have already been reversed at that point: fix the data and re-run the
downgrade, or run airflow db migrate to return to 3.4.

On MySQL a failure after those checks leaves the schema partly downgraded,
as MySQL cannot roll back DDL. Taking a backup before attempting the
downgrade on MySQL is advised, so it can be restored in that case.

Dag Importer for non-Python Dags (#72369, #73728, #73853, #74020, #74084, #74333, #74586)

Airflow 3.4.0 can author an entire Dag - schedule, tasks, and dependencies - in a language other
than Python. AIP-85 adds a pluggable Dag Importer in the Task SDK that teaches the Dag processor to
recognize source formats beyond .py: each format registers an importer, the processor runs the
matching language runtime, and the resulting Dags surface in Airflow like Python Dags. The formats
that land on it are the TypeScript, Go, and Java language SDKs and a native YAML Dag format (a
.yaml file with a $schema marker, validated against a schema and built into real operators,
with explicit templating). The Dag Importer framework and the language SDKs are experimental in 3.4
and their APIs may change.

For detailed usage instructions, see :doc:/administration-and-deployment/dag-importers.

Unify executor workload queues under BaseExecutor.executor_queues (#63491)

Executor workload state is now stored on the unified BaseExecutor.executor_queues mapping keyed
by WorkloadType and scheduled through trigger_workloads. The previous per-type attributes
and entrypoints (queued_tasks, queued_callbacks, supports_callbacks, trigger_tasks,
order_queued_tasks_by_priority) and the Airflow 3.3 connection-test surface are folded into
this mapping and kept as backward-compatible shims that emit RemovedInAirflow4Warning (to be
removed in Airflow 4.0). Out-of-tree executors should declare supported_workload_types and
implement trigger_workloads. Connection tests are now admitted under the same per-heartbeat
budget as tasks and prioritized ahead of them. See
#63491 <https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/63491>_ for the full migration guide.

psycopg3 is now the default Postgres driver (#68496)

psycopg3 (psycopg) is now the default driver for the metadata database, for both the sync and
the async engine, replacing psycopg2 and asyncpg. A bare postgresql:// (or a legacy
postgres:// / postgres+psycopg2://) sql_alchemy_conn is rewritten to
postgresql+psycopg://, and the derived async URL uses postgresql+psycopg_async:// when
psycopg3 is installed (falling back to asyncpg otherwise). Airflow also disables psycopg3's
server-side statement preparation (prepare_threshold = None) so the metadata database works out
of the box behind transaction-mode PgBouncer, the recommended production setup. To keep psycopg2 or
asyncpg, install the apache-airflow-providers-postgres[psycopg2] / [asyncpg] extra and
configure the connection explicitly; see #68496 and #69469 for details, including how to re-enable
statement preparation.

Asset-triggered Dags create one run per event by default (#68517)

Single-asset schedules and asset OR expressions now create one Dag run per event instead of
consuming all queued events in one run. This also applies to AssetOrTimeSchedule and
PartitionedAssetTimetable.

To retain batching, set batch_asset_events=True on the timetable or enable [scheduler] batch_asset_events and reparse the affected Dags. Already serialized timetables without this
option retain their previous batching behavior until reparsed.

Schedules requiring several events, including schedule=[a, b], asset AND expressions, and
partitioned timetables using RollupMapper, continue to batch by default. Explicitly setting
batch_asset_events=False for these schedules raises a timetable validation error.

Custom graph colors return via ui_color and ui_fgcolor (#68760)

The ui_color and ui_fgcolor attributes on operators and TaskGroups color the graph view
again -- the node fill from ui_color and the operator label from ui_fgcolor, as they did in
Airflow 2. They were silently ignored since Airflow 3.0.

The value can be a raw color (a hex code like #e8b7e4 or a CSS name) or a Chakra theme token --
a palette token such as blue.500 or a semantic token such as brand.solid that adapts to
light and dark mode (including tokens added through custom UI theming); a token resolves through a
theme-controlled CSS variable. The node border keeps reflecting the task-instance run state; the
custom color is applied to the fill and label only.

validate_key now raises ValueError instead of AirflowException (#68890)

The airflow.utils.helpers.validate_key utility now raises ValueError instead of
AirflowException when an invalid key is provided (for example an invalid format or a
length-limit violation).

The deprecated Dataset alias has been removed from the airflow module (#70154)

Use Asset from airflow.sdk instead.

Audit log rows not tied to a Dag now require the AUDIT_LOGS_ALL view (#70759)

Rows in the audit log whose dag_id is NULL record operations that are not tied to a Dag,
such as Connection, Variable and Pool changes. They were returned to any caller that could read
event logs at all, because there is no per-Dag key to authorize them on and both read paths fell
back to a Dag-level audit log check.

They are now gated on a dedicated AccessView.AUDIT_LOGS_ALL, in the same way
AccessView.IMPORT_ERRORS_ALL gates import errors for files with no registered Dag. Rows bound
to a Dag keep their existing per-Dag check.

  • GET /eventLogs no longer returns rows with a NULL dag_id to callers without the new
    view, and excludes them from total_entries and pagination. GET /eventLogs/{event_log_id}
    returns 403 for such a row. An id matching no row still returns 404.
  • With the simple auth manager the view is granted to the ADMIN role only. With the FAB auth
    manager it maps to a new All Audit Logs resource, which ships in the Admin role; custom
    roles that need to read these rows must be granted All Audit Logs.can_read explicitly.
  • An auth manager that cannot map a requested AccessView now denies that view and emits a
    UserWarning instead of raising KeyError. This affects auth managers older than the core
    they run against, which previously failed the request with a server error.

Team names must now be lower case, and cannot contain two consecutive underscores (#70886)

airflow teams create and airflow teams sync now accept only names matching
(?!.*__)[a-z0-9_-]{3,50} -- lower case letters, digits, hyphens and single underscores. Upper
case letters and __ were previously accepted.

A team name is embedded in the AIRFLOW_CONN__<TEAM>___<ID> environment variable namespace that
holds team scoped secrets, and the backend upper-cases the name when it builds that variable.
data_eng and Data_Eng therefore resolved a single namespace between them, and a name
containing ___ could not be told apart from the separator.

airflow db migrate lower-cases every stored team name, moving that team's Dag bundles,
Connections, Variables, Pools and Triggers with it. Two stored names that differ only in case would
collapse onto one row and silently merge two teams, so migration refuses to start while any such
pair exists -- rename all but one first. Names that stay invalid for another reason, such as
containing __, are migrated as they are; they keep working, but airflow teams sync exits
non-zero until they are renamed.

Changes to how pending asset events trigger Dag runs (#70972)

Deleting asset event records with airflow db clean now also removes any asset events that are
still pending for a downstream Dag. This mainly affects Dags waiting on a multi-asset condition,
where a pending event can be purged before the condition is met. Deleting an asset event now
consistently means it will not trigger a run; previously such a pending trigger could still fire
after the event had been purged.

Relatedly, an asset event that was queued for a Dag while it was scheduled on that asset is still
used to trigger the run, and appears among the run's triggering events, even if the asset is later
removed from the Dag's schedule. Previously, they were silently dropped.

Callbacks now redeem a single-use token before they run (#71192)

A worker now redeems a callback's single-use token with the API server (PATCH /execution/callbacks/{callback_id}/run) before importing and running the callback. Redeeming the
token moves the callback from queued to running and swaps it for a short-lived execution-scoped
token. Before this change a callback ran without the worker making any authenticated call, so the
token minted for it was never checked.

Because the token is single-use, a redelivered or replayed message that reaches a callback that is
already running or finished is refused rather than run again. A worker on 3.4 needs an API server
that serves this endpoint; a worker talking to an older API server negotiates the API version and
behaves as though the endpoint is not there.

Clearing a task now discards its task state store entries by default (#72100)

Clearing a task instance now discards its task_state_store entries, so the next attempt starts
from the beginning instead of resuming from a checkpoint or reconnecting to an external job
recorded by the cleared attempt. Retries are unaffected and keep task state as before. This applies
to clearing individual task instances (the clear endpoint/dialog and airflowctl tasks/dags clear); clearing a whole Dag run still keeps task state (tracked in
#72929 <https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/72929>_). To preserve the old behaviour, pass
keep_task_state=True (or tick "keep task state" in the clear dialog; a per-browser default is
available under Settings > Clearing). Note a task-instance clear now also deletes
task_state_store rows for that task instance.

[core] execute_tasks_new_python_interpreter now applies to Airflow 3 task processes (#72164)

On Airflow 3 the option had no effect on task execution (only the Edge worker read it). When set to
True, the task supervisor now exec\ s a fresh interpreter right after forking the task
process, which prevents the fork from inheriting a lock held by a supervisor thread (a permanent
hang at the task's first TLS call). Deployments that kept the option True from Airflow 2 get
this behaviour, and its per-task interpreter start-up cost, on upgrade without further action; set
it to False to keep bare fork. The task process reads the global value, so a team-scoped Edge
setting alone does not turn it on. Edge workers with the option True already start a fresh
interpreter for the supervisor and will now start a second one for the task. The Dag processor, the
triggerer and task callbacks (which the callback supervisor runs from a closure that cannot be
named for an exec'd child) are not affected and keep bare fork.

Gracefully pause Dags by draining active runs (#72407, #73225, #73055, #73763)

Airflow now supports a draining scheduling state for Dags. Draining stops the scheduler from
creating new scheduled or asset-triggered Dag runs while allowing already queued and running Dag
runs to continue. Explicitly triggered runs remain allowed.

After outstanding Dag runs finish, the Dag automatically transitions to paused. Users can
cancel draining to return the Dag to active.

Manual runs, backfills and asset materializations on a paused Dag can drain the Dag instead of
unpausing it: choose Drain in the UI, or set drain_dag in the REST API request. Draining
lets unfinished runs of the Dag start or resume, except those held by paused backfills, creates no
scheduled runs, and pauses the Dag again once all unfinished runs finish. Paused backfills remain
paused and must be resumed for their runs to finish and draining to complete.

The UI, REST API, and airflowctl expose the active, draining, and paused scheduling
states, and the Dags list can pause, drain, or unpause several selected Dags at once. Existing
is_paused API usage remains supported; use scheduling_state when the draining state must be
selected or reported explicitly.

Reparsing a file with no registered Dag now requires the REPARSE_ALL view (#72896)

A file that failed to import before defining any Dag has no per-Dag key to authorize a reparse
against, so PUT /parseDagFile/{file_token} previously returned 404 for it. Reparsing such a
file is now gated on a dedicated AccessView.REPARSE_ALL -- a write action of its own, distinct
from the permission to view import errors -- and the Dag import errors modal gains a reparse action
for these files.

  • PUT /parseDagFile/{file_token} for a file with no registered Dag authorizes against
    REPARSE_ALL and returns 403 when the caller lacks it, instead of 404. A file that has
    a registered Dag keeps its existing per-Dag can_edit check.
  • With the simple auth manager the view is granted to the ADMIN role only. With the FAB auth
    manager it maps to a new All Reparses resource, which ships in the Admin role; custom
    roles that need to reparse such files must be granted All Reparses.can_read explicitly.

Removed the --file-io option from the airflow info command (#73054)

--file-io uploaded the report to file.io and printed a shareable link. file.io no longer
accepts anonymous uploads, so the option could not succeed; it also ended in an unhandled traceback
rather than reporting the failure.

Redirect the output instead::

airflow info --anonymize > airflow-info.txt

Note that --file-io applied --anonymize implicitly. Pass --anonymize explicitly when
sharing a report: plain airflow info prints connection strings, including passwords, in
cleartext.

Task heartbeats are no longer retried by [workers] execution_api_retries (#73244)

Heartbeats had two overlapping retry mechanisms: the Task SDK API client retried every request,
including heartbeats, and the supervisor separately counted consecutive heartbeat failures against
[workers] max_failed_heartbeats. The client retries also had the unwanted side-effect of
blocking the supervisor's monitor loop while it backed off, so during an API server outage the
supervisor would be delayed forwarding task logs and/or noticing that the task subprocess had
exited.

Heartbeat retries are now governed solely by max_failed_heartbeats, whose default has been
adjusted from 3 to 30 to keep roughly the same tolerance for an unreachable API server as
the two mechanisms combined gave before.

If you have set [workers] max_failed_heartbeats explicitly, you may wish reconsider value you
have chosen. It is now the whole retry budget: with the default [workers] min_heartbeat_interval of 5 seconds, the worker tolerates roughly 5 * max_failed_heartbeats
seconds of API unavailability before terminating a running task. You should likely keep the
resulting value below any configured [scheduler] task_instance_heartbeat_timeout (default 300
seconds).

Deadline alert callbacks validated at parse time; numeric intervals deprecated (#73294)

DeadlineAlert now refuses a callback that is not exactly AsyncCallback or
SyncCallback, so a subclass fails when the Dag is parsed rather than when the scheduler reads
it back. The scheduler decodes stored callbacks by exact class name so no class named by a Dag
author is imported or instantiated there, which means a subclass could be written and then never
read.

Passing a number as the interval is deprecated and now emits RemovedInAirflow4Warning. It
is still accepted and taken as a count of seconds, but the supported types are timedelta and
VariableInterval. A timedelta subclass such as pendulum.duration(...) is accepted and
normalized to a plain timedelta, where previously it passed validation and then failed during
serialization. interval=True is refused, because bool is an int subclass and would
otherwise be taken as one second.

The POST /assets/{asset_id}/materialize endpoint now requires a JSON request body (#73328)

Previously a request with no body was accepted and the asset was materialized with default values.
The endpoint now requires an explicit JSON body, consistent with the other mutating endpoints: a
request without a body is rejected with 422, and an empty HTML form is not a valid input
anymore. All body fields remain optional, so an empty object ({}) is a valid body.

TaskInstance try numbers now increase before the next try starts (#73554)

.. note::

If you have any external systems that look at task logs or TI state for an up-for-retry TI, you
will need to be aware of this change and update your code.

For example, if you made a request to GET /api/v2/dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{dag_run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id} expecting to get info about
the failed try, you will now need to look at GET /api/v2/dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{dag_run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id}/tries/{try_number - 1}

When a task is up_for_retry, try_number now identifies the upcoming try. To retrieve the try that
failed, request /tries/{try_number - 1}. The UI shows the pending try and provides a link to
the previous try's logs.

Airflow now allocates a task instance's UUID and try number together immutably so they consistently
identify the same try.

Previously when a task entered the retry cooldown period, it would be given a new UUID, but keep on
try number N and have the state of UP_FOR_RETRY until that period was up (at which point that try
would be marked FAILED and the try number incremented). Instead, the failed try is immediately
marked with state of FAILED, and a new try created in state UP_FOR_RETRY.

Deprecate cyclic TaskGroup dependencies (#73746)

A Dag whose TaskGroups depend on each other in a cycle, when each TaskGroup is treated as a single
unit, now issues a TaskGroupCycleDeprecationWarning at parse time and shows a Dag warning in
the UI that names the TaskGroups and tasks involved. These Dags still parse and run, because their
task dependencies are acyclic, but Airflow 3.5 is planned to reject them at parse time.

A dependency into or out of any task in a TaskGroup counts as a dependency of the whole group, so a
path that leaves a TaskGroup and comes back into it is a cycle. For example, a >> bridge >> b,
with a and b in the same TaskGroup and bridge outside it, makes the group depend on
bridge and bridge depend on the group, even if a >> b is also set.

  • Move tasks between TaskGroups, or out of them, so that each group depends on the others in one
    direction only. In the example above, move bridge into the group, or move b out of it.
  • To catch these Dags in CI, run your Dag tests with -W error::airflow.sdk.exceptions.TaskGroupCycleDeprecationWarning. The check runs when a Dag is
    added to a DagBag, so only tests that load your Dags into a DagBag and assert there are
    no import errors catch them; a test that only imports a Dag file does not.

See "Cyclic TaskGroup dependencies" in the Dags documentation.

Language SDK coordinators load task handlers from a Dag bundle (#73970)

The experimental jars_root (Java) and executables_root (Go) coordinator kwargs are removed.
Put the artifacts in a Dag bundle registered in [dag_processor] dag_bundle_config_list and set
task_handler_bundle_name in the coordinator's kwargs, or leave it unset to use the task's
own Dag bundle. A config that still sets a removed kwarg fails with Cannot instantiate coordinator '<key>'.

Support for Python 3.10 has been removed (#74151)

Airflow now requires Python 3.11 or newer. Python 3.10 reaches its end of life in October 2026, and
Airflow drops support for a Python version in main as soon as it reaches end of life. The
apache-airflow distribution, the Task SDK, airflowctl and all providers released from
main declare requires-python = ">=3.11".

Deprecate the required_kwargs attribute for custom deadline references (#70714)

Implement _evaluate_with() with a dagrun parameter instead.

CI and production images are now based on Docker Hardened Images and Debian 13 (#73038)

Airflow's CI and production images are now based on Docker Hardened Images <https://dhi.io>_ for
Python and Debian 13 "trixie".

Python is no longer compiled from source during the image build - it comes from the hardened base
image instead, which removes the source download, its signature verification and the compilation
itself from the build. Python still lives in /usr/python, which is now a symlink to the
/opt/python location the base image uses, so paths inside the image are unchanged.

The BASE_IMAGE build argument now defaults to
ghcr.io/apache/airflow/base/python:<version>-debian13-dev, Airflow's public mirror of the
upstream dhi.io/python image, so building an image needs no registry credentials. Anyone
overriding BASE_IMAGE with a plain debian:bookworm-slim image has to switch to an image that
already provides Python, or build the legacy flavor.

The base OS moved from Debian 12 "bookworm" to Debian 13 "trixie". Library packages renamed in
trixie's 64-bit time_t transition (for example libssl3 is now libssl3t64) have to be
updated in custom RUNTIME_APT_DEPS / ADDITIONAL_RUNTIME_APT_DEPS, and the MySQL-compatible
client now comes from MariaDB 11.8.

For the 3.4.x line, production images built the previous way - Python compiled from sources on
debian:bookworm-slim - are still published as the deprecated legacy flavor, selected with
the new AIRFLOW_IMAGE_FLAVOR="legacy" build argument. They will be removed in Airflow 3.5.0.

The PYTHON_LTO build argument is gone. To build a FIPS-compliant image, point BASE_IMAGE at a
FIPS variant of the hardened image instead, for example dhi.io/python:3.13.16-debian13-fips-dev.

Task SDK API client trusts the system certificate store instead of certifi (#73116)

With [api] client_use_public_certs enabled (the default), the Task SDK client that talks to the
Execution API now trusts the operating system's certificate store through truststore instead of
the certifi CA bundle. CAs from [api] ssl_ca_file and [api] ssl_cert are still trusted
in addition to the system store, and certifi is no longer a Task SDK dependency.

Workers must have the public CAs they rely on installed in the system store (for example, the
ca-certificates package on Debian-based images). On macOS and Windows, certificate validation
is delegated to the operating system, which can reject server certificates that OpenSSL accepted,
such as private-CA certificates without the serverAuth extended key usage.

Older workers can no longer resume deferred tasks whose next_kwargs hold custom classes (#73577)

When a deferred task resumes on a worker with an older Task SDK, the API server no longer reconstructs arbitrary classes from the stored next_kwargs to convert them to the legacy format. Built-in value types, assets and asset aliases (including asset access control) are still converted, without constructing them. A deferred task whose next_kwargs hold any other class now fails on such a worker with an error naming the type and asking to upgrade the Task SDK, instead of crashing on a payload it cannot decode.

What to do: if you run workers with apache-airflow-task-sdk 1.1.x or older and your deferrable operators or triggers pass instances of custom classes in next_kwargs (for example via self.defer(..., kwargs=...) or in the trigger event payload), upgrade the Task SDK on those workers to 1.2.0 or later. Newer workers receive next_kwargs unchanged and are not affected. Until all workers are upgraded, pass only built-in values, assets and asset aliases in next_kwargs of tasks that may resume on older workers.

Deadline Alert callback kwargs are decoded where the callback runs (#74830)

The keyword arguments of Deadline Alert callbacks are no longer decoded by the scheduler. They
are kept in their serialized form and decoded where the callback runs: by the triggerer for an
AsyncCallback, and by the callback runner on the worker for a SyncCallback.

Workers that run SyncCallback Deadline Alerts need a Task SDK that includes this change, so
upgrade apache-airflow and apache-airflow-task-sdk on workers together. A worker with
an upgraded apache-airflow and an older Task SDK fails such callbacks with an error instead
of running them. Callbacks created before the upgrade run as before.

Custom XCom backends that override serialize_value must implement store_value to support task loops (#74858)

Every iteration of a task inside a loop is its own task instance, but serialize_value
receives the same dag_id, run_id, task_id, map_index and key for all of
them, so a backend that builds its storage location from those makes every iteration's XCom
read back as the last iteration's value. Backends should override store_value and
load_value instead, and build the storage location with XComCoordinate.build_path,
which is unique per task instance, or per write when the write cannot know the task instance.

A Dag that uses a loop fails on startup when the configured XCom backend still stores values
through serialize_value, even if it already writes to a unique location. This includes
XComObjectStorageBackend from apache-airflow-providers-common-io 1.10.1 and earlier;
upgrade the provider before using task loops with it.

Custom Task State Store backends will likewise need to include
scope.region_id in their storage key to support mapped tasks inside a loop
and loop iterations regenerated by clearing.

airflow.utils.email is deprecated in favor of the SMTP provider (#75414)

The functions in airflow.utils.email (send_email, send_email_smtp, send_mime_email,
build_mime_message and get_email_address_list) now live in
airflow.providers.smtp.utils.emailer. The old names still work and raise a DeprecatedImportWarning.
Airflow now requires apache-airflow-providers-smtp>=3.2.0.

Keep [email] email_backend set to airflow.utils.email.send_email_smtp. Airflow treats that value as
"send task emails with SmtpNotifier", which reads all SMTP settings from the Connection. Changing it to
the provider path sends through the [smtp] settings instead.

If you call these functions directly:

  • The SMTP Connection is looked up with BaseHook.get_connection. A script that runs outside Airflow's
    processes needs the Connection in an environment variable or a secrets backend, not only in the metadata
    database.
  • Settings are read through the Task SDK configuration, so values changed at runtime with
    airflow.configuration.conf.set() are not seen. airflow.cfg and environment variables work as before.
  • Tests that patch airflow.utils.email.send_mime_email no longer intercept the call made by
    send_email_smtp. Patch airflow.providers.smtp.utils.emailer.send_mime_email instead.

  • The API server uses a second database connection pool

    API server workers now run some database work on the async engine as well as the sync one, and each engine has its own connection pool, sized by the same [database] sql_alchemy_pool_size and [database] sql_alchemy_max_overflow settings. What uses the async pool depends on the --apps option of airflow api-server:

    • execution: task heartbeats and several Execution API reads.
    • core: the audit log entry recorded for each write request through the REST API or the UI.
    • all (the default): both of the above.

    In every mode a worker can therefore open up to twice sql_alchemy_pool_size + sql_alchemy_max_overflow connections (30 with the defaults) and keep up to twice sql_alchemy_pool_size of them idle. Account for this, per [api] workers, when sizing PgBouncer or the database's max_connections.

    The async pool is used since #67800, #73403, #73407 and #76416. (#76430)

item.description:
oxc-project/oxc | 23363 stars| 1452 forks.

⚓ A collection of high-performance JavaScript tools.

🚀 Features

  • 4a52ba2 oxlint: Discover tsrs for type-aware linting (#28751) (camc314)
  • b7d2c75 linter/eslint/no-redeclare: Add ignoreDeclarationMerge option (#28816) (Cam McHenry)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • fa66fde oxlint,oxfmt: Resolve Vite+ config root from the config file directory (#28801) (MK (fengmk2))
  • 2091564 linter/jsdoc/require-param: Ignore enclosing function JSDoc (#28866) (camc314)
  • c6ec50b linter/react/only-export-components: Classify JSX values as non-components (#28761) (camc314)
  • 3c051ab linter/vitest/prefer-called-exactly-once-with: Preserve neighboring code in autofix (#28864) (camc314)
  • 674b962 linter/eslint/no-misleading-character-class: Use lazy regex for combining marks (#28822) (Sysix)
  • 838d339 linter/vitest/prefer-called-exactly-once-with: Avoid panic on non-ASCII text (#28850) (YT)
  • 8d24c26 linter/jsx-a11y/aria-role: Allow role={undefined} (#28804) (Abhay Godavarthy)
  • a7143bf linter/eslint/no-restricted-imports: Respect allowTypeImports correctly for empty patterns (#28842) (Cam McHenry)
  • 3d3a6f4 react-compiler: Ignore callback-local reassignments (#28820) (camc314)
  • 0cc6515 linter/unicorn/prefer-type-error: Report throws in unbraced if branches (#28819) (camc314)
  • ae43c80 linter/unicorn/prefer-single-call: Remove duplicate fix status (#28763) (Mikhail Baev)
  • a8a621a linter/eslint/no-fallthrough: Ignore unreachable exits from infinite loops (#28755) (camc314)
  • 7a17a80 linter/eslint/prefer-spread: Report calls on non-member expressions (#28753) (camc314)
  • 28442f7 oxlint: Prevent --init from overwriting existing configs (#28754) (camc314)
  • 0ae350d linter/unicorn/no-zero-fractions: Preserve exponent case (#28752) (camc314)
  • b5b3f3f linter/eslint/no-misleading-character-class: Detect more combining characters (#28733) (Sysix)

⚡ Performance

  • 74d50c1 linter: Overlap import graph batches instead of polling on a pool worker (#28323) (Dunqing)

item.title: [actix/actix-web] actix-web: v4.18.2
item.description:
actix/actix-web | 24928 stars| 1993 forks.

| Rust | JavaScript | Shell | Just |

Actix Web is a powerful, pragmatic, and extremely fast web framework for Rust.
  • Increase the default form payload limit to 32 KiB.
  • Bound decompressed request payloads using the same configured size limits for form, JSON, bytes, and string extractors. GHSA-qph8-7859-gq2f
  • Add UrlencodedError::OverflowUnknownLength error enum variant for form payloads that exceed the limit while streaming.
  • Add a UTF-8 encoded filename* parameter in ContentDisposition::attachment() for non-ASCII filenames.
  • Return 405 with an Allow header from the built-in app default when method guards reject matching resources, including macro routes.

item.title: [camsong/You-Dont-Need-jQuery] Release 3.0
item.description:
camsong/You-Dont-Need-jQuery | 20105 stars| 1702 forks.

| JavaScript |

Examples of how to do query, style, dom, ajax, event etc like jQuery with plain javascript.

The guide now targets evergreen browsers. Every snippet that was changed is checked against jQuery 4 by a test.

Breaking: Internet Explorer is no longer supported

Snippets target the latest Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and Opera. IE-specific fallbacks are gone: vendor-prefixed matchesSelector, the closest polyfill, Array.prototype.*.call, createEvent / initCustomEvent, pageYOffset, parentNode.removeChild. If you still need IE, use the last IE-compatible version or v2.0.

Native one-liners

jQuery Native
remove / insertBefore / insertAfter el.remove() / el.before() / el.after()
empty el.replaceChildren()
unwrap / replaceWith parent.replaceWith(...parent.childNodes) / el.replaceWith()
$(html) <template>
$.extend(true, …) structuredClone()
$.Deferred Promise.withResolvers()
scrollTop() window.scrollY
outerHeight() / outerWidth() el.offsetHeight / el.offsetWidth

New sections

  • Request JSON (with the response.ok gotcha), Post JSON, Abort and timeout
  • one → { once: true }, event delegation, removing several listeners at once with AbortController
  • async / await variants for always and then
  • Effects use the Web Animations API (el.animate()); slideUp / slideDown measure real height

Fixed snippets

Snippets that threw or disagreed with jQuery: nextAll / prevAll, :contains, append / prepend with HTML strings, clone (now deep), trigger, inArray, isPlainObject(null), merge, globalEval, parseHTML, Deferred, fadeOut, fadeTo, animate. Plus broken markdown, anchors and syntax errors in the README (#264).

Tests and tooling

  • Karma / webpack 1 / Babel 6 replaced with Vitest + jsdom; tests run in GitHub Actions on PRs and master
  • Travis CI config and badges removed (#263)

Translations

All 15 translations are synced with the current snippets (#268–#282).

item.title: [awslabs/llrt] v0.10.0-beta
item.description:
awslabs/llrt | 8833 stars| 401 forks.

| Makefile | JavaScript | Rust | TypeScript | CSS | HTML | Shell | C | Dockerfile |

LLRT (Low Latency Runtime) is an experimental, lightweight JavaScript runtime designed to address the growing demand for fast and efficient Serverless applications.

Features

  • Added textStream() to Blob, Request and Response (@nabetti1720)
  • Added latin1, binary, ascii and base64url encodings to Buffer (@arxhr007)
  • Added a MkDocs documentation site (@richarddavison)

Fixes

  • Honor totalLength in Buffer.concat (@arxhr007)
  • Fix structuredClone crashing on DataView and align structuredClone, URLSearchParams and Headers with the specification (@arxhr007)
  • Fix structuredClone transfer handling and Web Streams conformance (@nabetti1720)
  • Fix Streams edge cases uncovered by the expanded WPT coverage (@nabetti1720)
  • Fix encoding streams behavior and share the WTF-8 encoding logic (@nabetti1720)
  • Correct Windows-1252 and streaming decoder behavior (@nabetti1720)
  • Do not synthesize an Origin header in server-side fetch (@nabetti1720)
  • Combine repeated response header values in fetch (@dills122)
  • Normalize network access policy matching in fetch (@dills122)
  • Resolve relative redirects with canonical origins in fetch (@dills122)
  • Enforce LLRT_NET_ALLOW and LLRT_NET_DENY for sockets and dgram, including bare-host, IPv6 and unix-socket entries (@richarddavison)
  • Look up SDK service endpoints by package directory, fixing the endpoints for SecretsManager and Cognito Identity Provider (@richarddavison)
  • Fix cyclic CommonJS requires with normalized paths (@nabetti1720)
  • Resolve the module field as ESM and fix the bridge for CommonJS modules with no named exports (@nabetti1720)
  • Fix package subpath resolution with explicit extensions (@nabetti1720)
  • Keep leading parent segments and relative roots in path.join and path.normalize (@Arthur031221)
  • Ensure the console initializes primordials (@ahaoboy)
  • Fix WASI compilation (@andreiltd)
  • Refresh os.networkInterfaces() and the os.cpus() frequency on every call instead of returning the values captured on first use (@richarddavison)
  • Parse JSON containing lone surrogate escapes correctly with simd-json 0.19 (@richarddavison)
  • Avoid pulling in unused crypto backend dependencies (@dills122)

Maintenance

  • Make Intl/Temporal (intl402) and post-quantum algorithms (pqc) opt-in Cargo features, and reduce the release binary size by ~10% (11.5MB to 10.4MB on arm64 musl) with extra musl codegen/linker flags and de-genericized stream promise helpers (@richarddavison)
  • Replace the custom zig linker wrapper scripts with cargo-zigbuild (@richarddavison)
  • Upgrade rquickjs to 0.14 (@richarddavison)
  • Require rsa 0.10.0-rc.19 in llrt_crypto (@richarddavison)
  • Improve WPT harness compatibility and skip browser-only and invalid-URL WPT cases (@nabetti1720)
  • Stabilize console error-stack test fixtures (@dills122)
  • Dependency upgrades

Thanks for all the reports and contributors

Full list of changes:
v0.9.0-beta...v0.10.0-beta

item.title: [semgrep/semgrep] Release v1.184.0
item.description:
semgrep/semgrep | 17536 stars| 1154 forks.

| Makefile | OCaml | Standard ML | Python | JavaScript | C | Java | Shell | Dockerfile | Go |

Lightweight static analysis for many languages. Find bug variants with patterns that look like source code.

1.184.0 - 2026-11-05

### Added

  • PHP: Improved virtual call resolution for basic trait composition. (CODE-9176)
  • Supply Chain: a requirements.txt dependency declared as a version range (litellm>=1.10) or with no version (flask) now produces a finding for every advisory whose affected versions overlap the declared range, in both the Python and native resolvers. Such a finding has no single installed version to confirm, so it needs review. A range line next to a pinned copy of the same package produces no finding of its own, since the pinned copy names the installed version. (SC-4243)
  • Set SEMGREP_LOG_JSON_FILE to emit structured execution events with scan metadata alongside existing text output. (SMS-3670)

### Changed

  • Scans are slightly faster. The dataflow analyses build the name of each variable with a plain string join, and no longer with Printf and Format. On 6 open-source repos, the scan time was a median of 3% lower, with identical findings. (dataflow-variable-keys)

  • go grammar update (v0.25.0):

    • Go source parsing now supports generic type aliases, preserving type parameters, constraints, and alias semantics. Existing alias patterns can match these declarations; spelling generic parameter lists in rule patterns remains unsupported.
    • Go correctly parses unnamed map parameters and results in mixed signatures such as ([]string, int, map[int]int, error), allowing function patterns to match those signatures.
    • Go correctly represents chained indexing such as table[key][next] as nested index expressions, restoring matches for nested-index patterns.

    (go-v0.25.0)

### Fixed

  • Semgrep no longer logs credentials embedded in a proxy URL (for example
    HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:password@proxy:8080) when it reports the configured
    proxy settings. (proxy-log-redact-userinfo)
  • Logs and traces no longer include snippets of the scanned source code when a
    file fails to parse. Parsing exceptions now report the file, line, column, and
    the length of the unexpected text instead. Dependency resolution errors for
    malformed lockfiles are reported the same way. (redact-source-in-telemetry)
  • pro: Reduced peak memory for large projects (CODE-10136)
  • Supply Chain: the yarn v1 lockfile parser no longer reports a package named
    "dependencies" with an empty version when a blank line precedes the
    dependencies block of an entry, and it now keeps that entry's dependency
    edges. Entries without a version line are reported as parser errors instead
    of dependencies with an empty version. (SC-4214)
  • Gradle module attribution now works for modules whose logical project name
    does not match their directory (a renamed include or a remapped
    projectDir in settings.gradle). The resolver's init script reports each
    project's actual build file, and dependencies are attributed to that file
    instead of falling back to the root manifest. (SC-4327)
  • semgrep ci --no-suppress-errors with --allow-local-builds: when dependency resolution fails and the scan exits with code 2, the reason is now also in the errors of the JSON output (one entry per resolver error or lockfile parse error of each failed subproject, or a generic entry if none was reported; resolver errors include the failed command and the end of its output, with common credential shapes such as URL credentials and Authorization headers redacted), not only in the log. Previously the JSON had no error, so pipelines that read it could not tell why the scan failed. (SC-4348)

item.title: [microsoft/playwright] v1.65.0
item.description:
microsoft/playwright | 99518 stars| 6810 forks.

| JavaScript | Shell | TypeScript | HTML | CSS | Batchfile | Objective-C | Makefile | CMake | C++ |

Playwright is a framework for Web Testing and Automation. It allows testing Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with a single API.

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    ['failures'],
    ['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
  ],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

    test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});

  • New PLAYWRIGHT_TRANSFORM_CACHE_DIR environment variable sets the directory for transpiled test files, for example on a Linux machine shared with other users.

New APIs

  • New options timeout and signal in cdpSession.send().
  • New testRun.mode() returns the execution mode of a suite during reporter.preprocess().

Breaking Changes ⚠️

  • TypeScript class fields now follow useDefineForClassFields from your tsconfig.json, the same as tsc. It is enabled for ES2022 and later targets, and when target is not specified. A field initializer that reads a constructor parameter property now fails, because the initializer runs first:

    class LoginPage {
  // TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getByRole')
  readonly submit = this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });

  constructor(private readonly page: Page) {}
}

    Move the initialization to the constructor, or set "useDefineForClassFields": false in your tsconfig.json.

  • Actions such as locator.click(), locator.check(), locator.tap(), locator.fill(), locator.clear() and locator.selectOption() now wait for the element to be not inert. An action on an element with the inert attribute, or inside such an element, now times out if the element stays inert.

  • A sharded run now fails with "No tests found" when no tests match across all shards. Pass --pass-with-no-tests to allow this. An empty shard still passes when other shards have tests.

  • Cookie matching now follows RFC 6265. With a URL, browserContext.cookies() and apiRequestContext.cookies() no longer return host-only cookies for subdomains or Path=/api cookies for /apiv2, and a Path=/foo/ cookie does not match /foo. APIRequestContext sends a cookie without a name as Cookie: x instead of Cookie: =x, and stores Set-Cookie: token as a cookie without a name.

  • Proxy credentials are no longer sent to websites. The credentials in the proxy option now answer only proxy challenges. To authenticate on a website, use httpCredentials.

  • Text that the browser does not render, such as text that is not assigned to a slot or text directly inside a closed <details>, is no longer part of accessible names and aria snapshots. This can change the results of page.getByRole() with a name, locator.ariaSnapshot() and expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot().

  • String and URLSearchParams values of the params option in APIRequestContext requests are now appended to the query that the URL already has, instead of replacing it.

  • .css, .less and .scss imports in test files now load as empty modules instead of being removed, so the imported file must exist.

  • The blob reporter again deletes the content of its output directory before it writes the report. Playwright 1.64 kept reports with other names.

  • Test locations of imported calls such as test( in CommonJS output now point to the start of the callee, for example a.spec.ts:3:7 instead of a.spec.ts:3:11. This is the same as in ESM.

Announcements

  • ⚠️ Playwright no longer tests on Node.js 20. Use Node.js 22, 24 or 26, as listed in the system requirements.
  • 🐳 Docker images now include Node.js 26 instead of Node.js 24, and the latest patch of Chromium on the same branch.

Browser Versions

  • Chromium 158.0.8127.18
  • Mozilla Firefox 159.0
  • WebKit 27.2

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:

  • Google Chrome 157
  • Microsoft Edge 156

item.title: [bazelbuild/bazel] 9.3.2
item.description:
bazelbuild/bazel | 26061 stars| 4678 forks.

| Shell | Python | C++ | Java | HTML | C | Makefile | PowerShell | Objective-C | Batchfile |

a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

Note

If you are looking for rolling releases, please visit this page.

Release 9.3.2 (2026-11-05)

Bazel 9.3.2 is a patch LTS release. It is fully backward compatible with Bazel 9 releases starting from 9.0.1; see Bazel 9.0.1 release notes for a note on backward compatibility.

  • Fixed an issue where Bazel occasionally hangs during external repo fetch. (#32159)

  • Reverted the change "Invalidate cached action execution results when remote cache/executor endpoints or --remote_instance_name change between invocations" introduced in 9.3.0; it was causing overeager invalidations, especially as action rewinding is now enabled by default. (#32254)

Acknowledgments

This release contains contributions from Fabian Meumertzheim and James Judd.

Notice: Bazel installers contain binaries licensed under the GPLv2 with Classpath exception. Those installers should always be redistributed along with the source code.

Some versions of Bazel contain a bundled version of OpenJDK. The license of the bundled OpenJDK and other open-source components can be displayed by running the command bazel license. The vendor and version information of the bundled OpenJDK can be displayed by running the command bazel info java-runtime. The binaries and source-code of the bundled OpenJDK can be downloaded from our mirror server.

Security: All our binaries are signed with our public key 3D5919B448457EE0.

item.title: [tavianator/bfs] Version 4.1.6
item.description:
tavianator/bfs | 1282 stars| 44 forks.

| Makefile | C | Shell |

A breadth-first version of the UNIX find command

Bug fixes

  • Fixed optimizer bugs that could produce wrong results for expressions involving the comma operator, like

    $ bfs \( -type f -o -type d \) , \! -type d

    The bugs were originally introduced in bfs 3.1 (February 6, 2024). (9b36c6bf, b6a703a3)

  • Fixed -regex with Oniguruma when a partial match was found before a complete one. For example, -regex '.*/a*\(ab\)*' failed to match ./aab. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 2.4 (February 22, 2022). (90bd8929)

  • Fixed -fstype on Linux bind mounts of the same file system. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 4.0.6 (February 26, 2025). (6fd62172)

  • Fixed -perm with multiple actions in a single symbolic mode, like +r+w, which only applied the file creation mask to the first action. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 4.0 (August 16, 2024). (0b16a06b)

  • Fixed -hidden and -nohidden with root paths like ./ or ../, which are now treated the same as . and ... The bug was originally introduced in bfs 2.2 (March 6, 2021). (95e9fec5)

  • Signals that were ignored at startup (for example by nohup) now stay ignored, both by bfs itself and by any child processes it spawns. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 3.3 (May 28, 2024). (3da97069)

  • Fixed -execdir ... {} + detection of a changed working directory with -depth and multiple root paths. The bug had been present since -execdir was implemented in bfs 1.0 (April 24, 2017). (c855df75)

  • Fixed an assertion failure after -execdir failed to open a parent directory. -execdir now also works in directories that are searchable but not readable. (f330325b)

  • Fixed -exec, etc. attempting to execute a directory if it appeared earlier in $PATH than the actual binary. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 2.3 (November 25, 2021). (a44963fe)

  • Fixed integer overflow in -mtime and friends with very large time units, which are now reported as an error (b7bd6b7d)

  • Fixed a potential crash when hiding the -status bar with SIGINFO/SIGUSR1. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 4.0.3 (October 22, 2024). (f63154bf)

  • Fixed a use-after-free in -D exec with commands like -exec {} +. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 1.2.3 (July 15, 2018). (d68703db)

  • Fixed spurious EMFILE errors by waiting for pending I/O before retrying. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 3.0 (July 13, 2023). (b5361674)

  • Fixed duplicate error messages for files that couldn't be stat()ed with -S {ids,eds} (b79d51a4)

  • Fixed error messages when fork() fails. The bug was originally introduced in bfs 4.0 (August 16, 2024). (07ddac5c)

  • Fixed coloring of dataless files on macOS (a96e7570)

  • Fixed -acl on DragonFly BSD (fc37d66c)
